items.title: Public Meeting to Consider A Proposed Development Charges
notes: Background Study and By-law

items.title: Mayor Watters welcomed everyone to the public meeting of Council
notes: under Section 12 of the Development Charges Act, 1997, as amended.

Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of this public meeting is to give the public an opportunity to ask questions, provide comments, and make representations on the Development Charges Background Study and proposed by-law. Council will not be taking any action on this report or by-law at this time.
Mayor Watters stated the DC Background Study and By-law were posted on the Township website on December 19, 2025. A media release and social media posts were released on the same day.
Mayor Watters advised notice was given in the Wellington Advertiser, a local newspaper, on January 8, 2026, and a developer virtual meeting occurred on January 21, 2026.
Mayor Watters called on Daryl Abbs, Partner, Watson & Associates Economists Ltd., to do a brief presentation regarding the study and the draft by-law.

Daryl Abbs, Partner, Watson & Associates Economists Ltd., provided a development charges (DC) overview, outlined recent changes to the Development Charges Act, the DC implementation policy, the growth forecast summary and the proposed rates and policies. He outlined the next steps, including the adoption of the by-law at the March 23rd Council meeting.
Mayor Watters indicated written comments received to date are attached to Report CAO2026-02 dated February 9, 2026.
Mayor Watters asked if anyone present wishes to speak at this time. He asked that delegations to provide their name and adhere to the 5 minute presentation rule.
DELEGATIONS

Joe Harris, Grand Highlands Home Builders Association requested Council prioritize projects and expenditures that support the core infrastructure necessary to enable new housing and growth – specifically roads, wastewater, and water. He indicated now is not the right time to increase development charges, an increase in DCs would further impact project viability, delay or cancel planned developments in the Township, and ultimately slow the delivery of much-needed housing.
He respectfully requested Council consider deferring a decision to afford the industry additional time to review options.

Joseph Puopolo, Polocorp Inc., supported the comments of Mr. Harris related to the housing crisis and housing costs and expressed concerns with the DC background study and by-law related to the urban boundary expansions. He did not want to see a two-tiered system of lands that may be within or added to the urban boundary resulting in development charges and perhaps a second class of lands coming in through another mechanism.

Marcus Gagliardi, Senior Land Development Manager, indicated there are lands owned by Cachet Homes inside and outside the current urban affected by the DC projects pushed out to 2034 and 2035 that doesn’t fall in line with the servicing program to bring those lands on-line. He requested those projects to be brought back to the 20231 time-line to align with the need for services and development. He noted housing is expensive and all demographics are struggling to afford to own a home and he reiterated the absorption of the DC increase cannot solely land on the developer.

Staff and the consultant responded to questions regarding the rates related to apartment buildings and muti-residential units, affordable versus attainable housing, deferral options and the cost and the responsibility for any updates to Township studies.
Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and declared the public meeting adjourned.
Mayor Watters called for a 5 minute recess.

items.title: Confederation Park Revitalization Plan
notes: Report from L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks

L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks provided an overview of the report, indicating the goals for Confederation Park included a) lead a community design process, b) develop a revitalization plan design and guiding document and c) inform the Township and Council of potential design options and adaptations.

Kara Singbeil and Mandy Cadger, GSP provided an overview of the community engagement undertaken and the guiding principles developed. They outlined the revitalization plan and implementation strategy, including the community priorities, costing & funding and the flexible timelines. They highlighted the various park improvements, the suggested materials to use and the budget and phasing outline.
Lucas Rogerson, Manage of Parks outlined the next steps, including activation of the phase 1 recommendations within the $150,000 budget.

Staff and the consultants responded to questions regarding the removal and replacement of the invasive species, trimming trees to preserve the look out and sightline enhancement, other funding sources and potential community partners, improved signage at the boat launch, lighting, and the redesign of the play structure to include all types of play.
